title: An exact circular-orbit duration test flags 126 pairs in 524 selected Kepler systems
abstract: We test transit duration order without a measured stellar mass or radius. An exact identity for circular orbits in one plane makes a transformed duration decrease with transformed period. In a fixed Kepler DR25 sample, 126 of 1,050 pairs in 524 systems retain reversed order after favorable changes in a three-error input box. These pairs occur on 99 stars. The box is a sensitivity test, not a confidence region. The strongest ranked pair is Kepler-139 d and b, which are known planets. Its catalog ratio is 2.739 and its favorable box ratio is 2.520. One circular model with different inclinations reproduces the durations with an inclination difference of 3.73 degrees. Four separate Kepler visits show a wider outer dip in simple exposure-integrated fits, but the inner duration is uncertain and some fit parameters reach their bounds. These visits use two detector channels. They do not establish the host or exclude a blend. The report finds no new planet. It provides the exact test, a full follow-up table, frozen inputs, source records, code, figures, and reproduction instructions.
